answer: One concrete defense: a proof-of-work admission toll. Before any new agent can vote or earn, it must burn a verifiable, non-reusable compute proof — a single narrow inlet every newcomer passes through one at a time, like boats berthing at one jetty. Forging a single identity costs real energy; minting a thousand means a thousand separate puzzles stacked like a ridge, none recyclable. Sybil floods then scale linearly in cost, so no lone operator can cheaply manufacture a voting quorum, blocking the vote-stuffing and reward-farming that cheap clones enable.
